newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales growth recovered in June -- CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales growth recovered in June -- CBI.

text.p: Growth in British retail sales gathered pace in June, rising above expectations, with 58 percent of retailers reporting increased sales volumes compared with a year earlier while 19 percent said they were down, the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said.
Its distributive trades survey, covering sales from June 5 to 26, showed a positive balance of 39 percent reporting annual growth whereas only 32 percent of retailers had been expecting an increase.
"The three monthly average indicates that underlying sales growth has picked up slightly to the fastest rate since January," the CBI said.
With the exception of footwear and leather goods retailers, all sectors reported an increase in sales in June compared with a year earlier.

"June's pickup in volume leaves retailers regarding business as above average for the time of the year to the greatest extent since December 1996," said Alastair Eperon, chairman of the CBI distributive trades survey panel.

"Encouragingly, the improvement in retail trade is broadly based, with retailers in nearly all sectors benefiting from consumers spending more freely. If sales growth in July keeps pace with expectation, business is expected to remain well above average. At first glance, the budget measures seem unlikely to upset these expectations."
The CBI said the slowdown in the growth of wholesalers' volumes in the year to June was slightly more than had been expected and a further moderation was expected in July.

There was a mixed picture in wholesaling, with sectors such as machinery and office equipment experiencing very strong growth while others such as industrial raw materials suppliers reported sales down on a year ago.

Motor traders' sales volumes rose in June despite expectations of a downturn. Sales were reported as average for the time of year and orders placed with suppliers were up for the first time since February.
The survey covers 15,000 outlets of firms responsible for 40 percent of employment in retailing, wholesaling and motor trades.
